rationale: The parameter-honesty pair of the R7 wave (M60.R7, the register's csharp entry `pType = … || this.extractTypeString(p) || "unknown"`), plus the same class in the fix's own new code. Three measured shapes, all of them a field holding something that is not what the field claims. (1) VARARGS WERE DROPPED: `params T[] name` is the one shape tree-sitter-c-sharp does not wrap in a `parameter` node — the `params` token, the array_type and the identifier are direct children of the parameter_list (script/m14/tmp/cs-params-modifier.ts) — so the named-`parameter` loop published NO parameter for it, and the loss was silent. Measured here: ParamsArray now publishes `rest:object[]`, ParamsAfterPlain `a:int, rest:string[]`, ParamsBuiltin `nums:int[]`. (2) NO PLACEHOLDER TYPE: `MissingLastType(int a, b)` and `MissingFirstType(a, int b)` are lists the recovery accepts with a missing type; the old code published `type: "unknown"` for the first and the parameter's OWN NAME for the second (extractTypeString's last-resort scan returns `b` / `a`), measured with script/m14/tmp/cs-param-type-probe.ts. Both now publish the parameter with NO type key at all. (3) NO BLANK NAME: for a nameless `params` parameter the grammar still inserts an empty `identifier` child (script/m14/tmp/cs-param-noname-tree.ts), so reading its text published `{ name: "" }`; measured here, NamelessParams now publishes NO parameter. The WELL-FORMED methods are the control — the fix may not degenerate into dropping varargs or dropping unresolvable-type parameters, which the `expect*` pins below enforce. Only reachable-on-recovery shapes are here, so the fixture carries a parse warning on purpose, exactly like csharp/literal-callee-recovery.

expectParameters.comment: control: the ordinary list is unchanged by the round
the varargs parameter the named-only loop dropped entirely; the array type IS the published type, the way java models varargs
a plain parameter followed by varargs: the loss was per-parameter, not per-list

the control that separates the two array shapes: an ORDINARY array parameter was published before this round too (it IS wrapped in a `parameter` node), so the varargs fix must not become `drop array-typed parameters`

control: the parameter still EXISTS with its real name; only the type is absent (`type` omitted here is the absence, not an unchecked key — the forbidParameters entry below is what convicts a reverted placeholder)
the type-less parameter is the FIRST one, so the damage is not positional
control: a nameless `params` parameter publishes nothing at all — the source writes no name, so there is no parameter to name

forbidParameters.note: the pre-fix pair: the placeholder literal `"unknown"`, and `"b"` — the parameter's OWN NAME returned by extractTypeString's last-resort scan. R7's class is a value in a name/value-bearing field that is not that value; a type field holding a name is the same defect one step worse.
the same class on the first position

the blank-name fabrication the params branch itself could publish: the grammar's recovery inserts an empty `identifier` child, so the node's text is "" and a name-bearing field then holds a blank — and the module's older fallback (`|| "anonymous"`) is the same class of invented name, so neither may appear for a parameter the source never names
the name-side placeholders: an unresolved type must not become an invented NAME either (the c lane's `name: "unknown"` is this exact shape, found by the same register)
